title: Machine learning identified local environmental associations with malaria-vector biting rates in Burkina Faso
summary: Interpretable machine-learning models applied to 15 months of field observations identified environmental variables associated with biting rates of malaria-vector species at local scales. The analysis is observational and does not show that changing those variables reduces transmission.
ai_technology: Interpretable machine-learning models of field mosquito biting-rate observations.
organization: Not stated in the abstract reviewed

evidence.tested: Models analyzed 15 months of biting-rate and environmental observations and reported species-specific local associations.
evidence.unknown: Observational associations do not establish causality or intervention effectiveness.
evidence.ai_role: Interpretable machine-learning models of field mosquito biting-rate observations.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
